newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB discount rate cut Thursday seen unlikely.
newsitem.headline: SNB discount rate cut Thursday seen unlikely.

text.p: Swiss money market traders do not expect the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to lower the discount rate at its meeting on Thursday, believing the SNB would like to keep such a move in reserve to combat future Swiss franc gains.
"I do not think so," said one money market trader, asked if he expected a cut in the rate, now at 1.00 percent. The level matches a historic low seen in 1978/79.
The SNB is expected to let markets know if any immediate rate decision is reached Thursday by 1400 GMT.
The SNB's most recent discount rate change was a cut from 1.50 percent on September 26, 1996.
Swiss traders and economists believe the SNB has not completely ruled out a new cut.
But most believe the SNB will keep such a move as a last resort, should the Swiss franc strengthen further in the run-up to the start of the single European currency January 1, 1999.
The SNB also has flooded the money market with liquidity in the past week, leading to a sharp drop in short rates. A discount rate cut would have only muted impact, traders said.

One trader said he did not expect a discount cut even though Swiss money market rates were well below 1.00 percent on Wednesday, with tomorrow/next money at 0.5 to 0.625 percent, down sharply from levels above 1-1/2 percent in early May.

"We have seen that money market short term rates can trade for one or two months below the discount rate. The SNB has no real need to change the discount rate. Why should they play the last card with the discount?" the trader said.
Janwillem Acket, country economist for Switzerland at Swiss Bank Corp, also said he would be surprised if the Swiss cut the discount rate on Thursday.
He said the SNB had made a strong impression on markets already, noting the recent drop in Swiss money market rates.
He added the Swiss franc is also off its recent highs against the mark, viewed as the key currency for Swiss exports.

Mark/Swiss traded at about 83.40 Swiss centimes Wednesday afternoon, below its seven-month low of 82.35 on May 21. The mark rose last Wednesday after the SNB announced significant additions of liquidity to the market to counter franc strength.
"We are now really at a position which is more comfortable," Acket said, adding further measures now "would be like emptying your reserve ammunition."
Acket and some market participants also thought it would be poor timing for the SNB to lower its discount rate Thursday before conclusion of French elections Sunday.

On Wednesday, two top Swiss National Bank officials, president Hans Meyer and vice president Jean-Pierre Roth in separate speaking engagements left little doubt the SNB will stay its generous course long enough to ensure a recovery.
Meyer reminded reporters Wednesday that the discount rate has little real significance. The rate "is not an essential part of the SNB's monetary policy," he said.
"What really matters is what happens in the market," Meyer said.
